title: Theo Thinks 22% Bracket = 22% Tax 😂
description:
Theo earns $80K, lands in the 22% tax bracket, and decides he owes 22% of everything: $17,600. Nora walks him through it. The first $16,100 is covered by the standard deduction, the next slice is taxed at 10%, a big chunk at 12%, and only the last $13,500 is taxed at 22%. His real federal income tax bill: $8,770, about 11% of his salary. Theo's only worry now is what to complain about at parties.

Takeaway: your bracket is your top rate, not the rate on every dollar. Your effective rate is usually much lower.

What did you think your tax rate was before this? Tell us below 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration: single filer, $80,000 salary, standard deduction only, 2026 federal income tax brackets and $16,100 standard deduction (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32). Ignores state tax, Social Security/Medicare (FICA), credits and other deductions. This is not financial advice.
